claims.text: Al-, Ti-, and V-containing multicomponent alloys can qualify as lightweight alloys.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous single-phase microstructure.
A homogeneous single-phase lightweight alloy can retain low density.
A homogeneous or chemically disordered lightweight multicomponent alloy can exhibit high mechanical strength.
A homogeneous microstructure can contribute to high corrosion resistance.
A homogeneous single-phase lightweight alloy can exhibit excellent high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The homogeneous matrix forms a continuous, dense oxide film predominantly composed of Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3 during high-temperature exposure.
A continuous Al2O3- and/or Cr2O3-rich film is responsible for both superior corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Nanostructural chemical uniformity facilitates rapid and uniform passivation.
Lattice distortion enhances mechanical strength through solid-solution strengthening.
Increasing Cu content in an Al-Cr-Ti-V-Cu lightweight alloy promotes Cu segregation.
Cu segregation accelerates localized corrosion and lowers corrosion resistance in AlCrTiV0.5Cux alloys.
Elemental segregation produces discontinuities in the protective oxide film.
Oxide-film discontinuities generate localized galvanic cells.
Minor elemental segregation, including Cu-rich phases, reduces mechanical integrity.
Compared with a Cu-segregated baseline, a homogeneous alloy will have higher yield strength.
Compared with a Cu-segregated baseline, a homogeneous alloy will have a lower corrosion current density.
Compared with a Cu-segregated baseline, a homogeneous alloy will have slower oxidation kinetics and lower oxidation mass gain at 900 °C.
The multifunctional benefits cease when phase separation disrupts the homogeneous matrix.
The multifunctional benefits cease when processing fails to produce sufficient atomic mixing.

contradictions.description: The experiment describes the two series as having identical base compositions, but the segregated series is also assigned a deliberate increase in Cu content. They therefore cannot be compositionally identical, and processing effects are confounded with composition effects.
